conflicts.fact: Lesson 1 builds ½ab sin C using a right-angled triangle, and Lesson 2 derives Heron's formula from it, but the geometry of h = b sin C is inconsistent with the labelling used
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 first draws a right angle at B with b as hypotenuse AC, then moves the right angle to D with sin C = h/b; Lesson 1 'Learned' calls h the side opposite C in a right sub-triangle whose hypotenuse is b. These are consistent only in the second diagram, but the first diagram's 'h' is labelled alongside a and b in a triangle where AB would be the height.

Lessons 1, 4, 5 and 8 give 6 m × 4 m with 65°, but Lesson 4 and 5 report the area as ≈21.75 m², while 6×4×sin65° = 21.75 m²; Lesson 5 Diagram B gives a height of 3.63 m (4×sin65° = 3.63, consistent). No conflict in value, but Lesson 5's school garden in Kisumu uses a different shape (6.5 m × 4 m, 110°) and is not part of the courtyard.

Lesson 4 uses a kanga patch with diagonals 8 cm and 5 cm and a courtyard border tile with diagonals 12 cm and 9 cm, and describes rhombus fabric patches as courtyard border decoration; Lesson 5 uses a Gikomba kanga patch with diagonals 24 cm and 18 cm (sides 15.23 cm, angle 56°). The side 15.23 cm and angle 56° do not match diagonals 24 and 18 (sides would be 15 cm, angle ≈ 73.7°), so the two data sets are not consistent for the same rhombus.

conflicts.fact: Triangle C and number of triangular sections in the courtyard
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 mentions two labelled triangular sections (A and B); Lesson 3 gives Triangle C sides 4.2, 3.8, 5.1 m; Lesson 2 tags Section C as Heron's and the courtyard triangle as 8 m, 11 m, 65°. Lesson 2 says Section B is the sine-area triangle, but Lesson 2 uses the 8 m/11 m/65° triangle which Lesson 1 calls Triangle A.

conflicts.fact: Whether the pentagon is part of the courtyard / Formula Family Tree and the lesson count
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says the pentagon is a standalone vendor context separate from the courtyard, but Lesson 6 also says the Courtyard Model was annotated across 'all 8 lessons' and Lesson 7 places the pentagon in the Formula Family Tree descended from the courtyard formulas. Lesson 8 says the pentagon is standalone, not part of the courtyard, while the phenomenon lists only pentagon among 'every formula developed' as tools for the courtyard.

Lesson 6 Model Building says a vendor stacks 6 such trays, while the teacher notes say 'total for 6 tiles ≈ 836.2 cm²' (trays vs tiles); also the s = 9 cm tray is described as a 'second tray' while the learner side calls it the courtyard model margin item.

conflicts.fact: Hexagonal border: tile size and sine-area link
conflicts.versions: The phenomenon says hexagonal border tiles come in only one size and are stone tiles; Lesson 7 gives side 8 cm, while Lesson 4 refers to rhombus decorative tiles on the courtyard border and Lesson 5 uses 0.5 m square floor tiles for the stage. Lesson 7 also says the hexagon is a 'descendant of ½ab sin C' for equilateral triangles, but the Family Tree shows Heron's and the parallelogram descending from it in a linear chain.

Lesson 5 computes 21.75 ÷ 0.25 = 87 tiles, rounded up to 88; 21.75/0.25 = 87 exactly, so rounding up to 88 is not required by the calculation (21.7578… would give 87.03 → 88 only with unrounded area 21.7 + ). Lesson 4 and 5 use 21.75 as the area, so 87 would be the count.
